svg.text: CR-Track — VS Code extension, Claude CLI engine
Everything runs on the developer's machine. The extension orchestrates; a short-lived `claude -p` child process does the reviewing.
Two things leave the laptop: the CLI's own authenticated call, and the redacted report.
· Read / Grep / Glob only — no Write, no Bash
· Killed the moment the dev stages again
staged diff in · source files read for context
Called by the CLI, not by the extension
Authenticated as the developer's own account
Rate limits + billing are per developer
POSTed by the extension, after redaction
Never file contents, diffs, or secrets
Failure queues on disk and retries
Review happens while the developer is still writing. Nothing blocks until there is something genuinely blocking.
wait for the index to settle
diff piped on stdin, handle retained
Read / Grep / Glob inside the repo
filter by threshold, assign stable ids
fix, or override with a written reason
queues on failure — commit never blocked
One command per review. Every constraint is a flag, not a paragraph of prompt text.
spawned by the extension — never shown to the developer

text.tspan: # Windows caps a command line at ~32,000 chars

svg.text: Hard read-only. No Write, no Bash, no network from the model — enforced, not requested.
Validated findings or a loud failure. Deletes the whole parse-and-retry loop.
Ruleset and language guides ship with the extension and version with it.
Per-review ceiling. A runaway review cannot drain a developer's day.
Reviews stay out of the developer's own session history.
The only way large diffs survive on Windows.
First run, and how it fails
The CLI is a dependency you do not control. Treat every failure as “review skipped”, never “commit blocked”.
PATH → known install dirs → claude.path setting
below the pinned minimum → stay dormant
not logged in → prompt once, never nag again
Fails safe — the commit always wins
skip, queue the report, commit proceeds
